title: The ALMA-QUARKS Survey. II. The ACA 1.3 mm Continuum Source Catalog and the Assembly of Dense Gas in Massive Star-Forming Clumps
question: How dense gas is assembled in massive clumps: build the QUARKS ACA 1.3 mm continuum source catalog (physical parameters) and test clump-fragment mass correlation, dense gas fraction and its evolution, and limited fragmentation

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image ACA continuum and line data
recipe.method: ALMA pipeline calibration, line-channel flagging with a model-spectrum mask, uvcontsub, then tclean with auto-multithresh
key_parameters: uvcontsub linear fit (order 1); line channels flagged using model spectrum widened to 50 km/s
briggs robust 0.5; noisethreshold 5 sigma; sidelobethreshold 1.25 sigma; line cubes multiscale [0,5,15]; pblimit 0.2; image 108x108 pix, 1 arcsec cell
edge channels (~2x128 per SPW) flagged in the first data release; no self-calibration

recipe.goal: Extract 1.3 mm continuum sources and measure fluxes
recipe.method: SExtractor on background-subtracted unpbcor continuum map with local rms map; fluxes divided by the primary beam response at barycenter/peak
key_parameters: background clipping at 3 sigma in boxes equal to the maximum recoverable scale
deblend_nthresh = 512, deblend_cont = 1e-5, minarea = effective beam size
assumptions: missing flux ignored because maximum observed source size (~14 arcsec) is about half the MRS

recipe.goal: Fit p-H2CO triplet for kinetic temperature and line width
recipe.method: five-parameter pyspeckit model on source-averaged SPW1 spectra, using a pre-computed RADEX non-LTE grid
key_parameters: free parameters: Tkin, log N(H2CO), log n(H2), v_lsr, FWHM; single velocity component
RADEX grid with line gradient fixed at 5 km/s/pc and Wiesenfeld & Faure collision rates
failed fits (seven spectra) assigned the clump-averaged dust temperature

recipe.goal: Derive source mass, size, densities, turbulence and Mach number
recipe.method: optically thin single-temperature dust mass formula, deconvolved size, N_H2, surface and volume density, thermal and non-thermal velocity dispersions, 3D Mach number
key_parameters: kappa = 1 cm2/g at ~230 GHz (Ossenkopf & Henning 1994, thin ice mantles)
mu_H2 = 2.81; mu_p = 2.37; channel width 1.34 km/s; m_H2CO = 30 m_H
30 sources with line width > 7 km/s (outflow wings) assigned an averaged observed velocity dispersion of 1.66 km/s
assumptions: dust temperature of each ACA source equals the H2CO kinetic temperature
distance uncertainty 20% and flux calibration uncertainty 10% included in mass errors

recipe.goal: Fit mass-radius and clump-fragment mass relations
recipe.method: linear regression in log space of M-R for clumps and fragments, and of Msource,max and Msource,total against Mclump
key_parameters: distance bins for robustness: <=3 kpc, 3-6 kpc, >6 kpc
assumptions: clump masses from SED fitting scaled to the updated distances

recipe.goal: Compute dense gas fraction and its dependence on size and L/M
recipe.method: DGF = summed ACA source mass in a clump / clump mass; compared against clump radius and L/M with a QUARKS plus ASHES combined sample
key_parameters: ASHES continuum images cropped to the QUARKS field size
linear regression on combined sample in log(DGF) vs log(L/M)

recipe.goal: Cross-match ACA sources with ATOMS 3 mm dense cores
recipe.method: elliptical mask from each ACA source geometry; an ATOMS core inside it defines a QUARKS-ATOMS link, with a fidelity value

score_reason: Project codes, imaging parameters, SExtractor settings, mass formulae and many numeric results are given, but clump masses, distances, line masks, several tclean parameters and fit/regression details are inherited or missing, and the catalog depends on external tables.
rediscovery_reason: ALMA ACA data under stated project codes are archive data, imaging and extraction recipe is largely explicit, and key results are numeric (207 sources, DGF 6%, regression coefficients), though external clump tables are needed.
